title: Agentic retrieval and Foundry IQ
summary: Agentic retrieval in Azure AI Search plans focused subqueries with an LLM, runs them in parallel across knowledge sources and merges the reranked results. Foundry IQ packages knowledge bases for agents.
useIf: Questions are multi-part or depend on chat history, you can accept preview features and an extra planning call, and you want an activity log and references.
avoidIf: You need GA-only features beyond minimal extractive retrieval, questions are single-fact lookups, or latency leaves no room for planning.

explain.md: In classic RAG your code builds the query. In **agentic retrieval** the app calls a **knowledge base** with the `retrieve` action and passes the query plus chat history. At `low` and `medium` effort an LLM plans focused subqueries and picks **knowledge sources**. All subqueries run in parallel (keyword, vector or hybrid), each is semantically reranked and the results are merged. Merged content is always returned. Source references and an execution `activity` log are optional (`includeActivity: true`). You need one knowledge base and at least one knowledge source [[r4]] [[r6]].

explain.title: Agentic retrieval request path
explain.alt: The app sends a query and chat history to a knowledge base, a planner model writes subqueries, sources are searched in parallel and reranked, and merged content with references and activity returns.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as App or agent
  participant K as Knowledge base
  participant P as Planner LLM
  participant S as Knowledge sources
  A->>K: retrieve query and history
  K->>P: Plan subqueries
  P-->>K: Subqueries and sources
  K->>S: Parallel searches and rerank
  S-->>K: Ranked results
  K-->>A: Merged content, references, activity

explain.caption: Reasoning effort (preview, checked 2026-10-13)
head: Effort
What happens
Notes
rows: No LLM planning, searches every source in the knowledge base
`outputMode` must be `extractiveData`, no answer synthesis or web source, up to 10 sources. The only effort in stable `2026-04-01`
5,000 answer tokens, 50 docs to semantic ranking (10 with L3 classification)
Adds a semantic classifier and one retry with a revised plan
10,000 answer tokens, 20 docs with L3, select regions only (15 listed)
Light first pass, escalates up to medium
Needs `2026-08-01-preview` and a model on the knowledge base

explain.md: Set effort on the knowledge base and override per request with `retrievalReasoningEffort.kind` [[r5]]. In the stable API only `intents` input, `minimal` effort and extractive output exist. Planning, answer synthesis, `messages` input, `auto` and SSE streaming need `2026-08-01-preview` [[r4]]. `maxRuntimeInSeconds` runs 10 to 600, default 90 [[r38]]. Search bills retrieval tokens, and Azure OpenAI bills planning and answer-synthesis tokens separately. Planner models include the `gpt-5` family, and the page updated 2026-09-17 marks GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 families deprecated [[r39]].

**Foundry IQ** is the managed knowledge layer: one knowledge base can serve many agents (Foundry Agent Service, Microsoft Agent Framework, custom apps through the Search REST API). Sources include Blob, SharePoint, OneLake and the public web, with chunking, embeddings and metadata extraction automated for indexed sources [[r7]]. **Azure OpenAI On Your Data retires on 2026-10-14**, and Microsoft recommends Foundry Agent Service with Foundry IQ [[r33]].

explain.title: Identity fails open
explain.md: For indexed sources, ACLs must be ingested (`ingestionPermissionOptions`) and the user token passed in `x-ms-query-source-authorization`. Omit the identity and indexed sources return unfiltered results. If `ingestionPermissionOptions` was not set at creation, results are unfiltered whatever the header says [[r6]].

whereToUse: Assistants that field multi-part questions across SharePoint, Blob and web sources
Agents that share one managed knowledge base instead of each owning an index
Systems that need references and an activity log for audit and debugging
Teams migrating off Azure OpenAI On Your Data before its retirement

use: Questions have several parts or rely on earlier turns
Several knowledge sources must be searched and merged
Preview status is acceptable and pinned versions are managed
You want the planning and reranking inside the service
avoid: Your policy allows GA features only, which limits you to `minimal` extractive retrieval
Questions are simple lookups that one hybrid query answers
You cannot pass the user's identity to the retrieve call
flips: GA-only requirement: use classic hybrid plus semantic ranker, or `minimal` effort
Latency is tight: stay at `low` or below, and set `maxRuntimeInSeconds` deliberately
Planner model on the deprecated list: move to a `gpt-5` family model before relying on filters or hints

pitfalls.symptom: A caller sees documents they should not
pitfalls.cause: The retrieve call omitted the user token header, or ACLs were not ingested
pitfalls.fix: Set `ingestionPermissionOptions` at creation and always send `x-ms-query-source-authorization` [[r6]]

pitfalls.symptom: Code that worked on a preview version breaks
pitfalls.cause: Preview contracts changed: knowledge agents became knowledge bases, and docs show both `maxOutputSize` and `maxOutputSizeInTokens`
pitfalls.fix: Pin the API version, read the migration page and check the SDK spelling [[r34]]

scenarios.title: GA-only governance
scenarios.situation: A regulated team may only use generally available features. Users ask multi-part questions, and the current system is a single hybrid query.
unknowns: Can the team build its own decomposition step?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Keep classic hybrid plus semantic ranker, add application-side decomposition, and revisit agentic planning when it is GA
options.why: In the stable `2026-04-01` API only `minimal` extractive retrieval exists, so planning is preview [[r4]].

options.name: Enable `low` effort in production
options.tradeoff: Right where preview features are allowed and pinned.

options.name: Use `minimal` effort with the stable API
options.why: Fits policy and covers several sources.
options.tradeoff: No planning or synthesis, so multi-part questions still need your logic.

flips.if: Preview is allowed in a sandbox first
flips.then: Pilot `low` effort there and compare recall on the multi-part slice.
Stay on classic hybrid plus semantic ranker, since planning adds latency and cost without a benefit.

scenarios.title: Multi-source copilot with permissions
scenarios.situation: An assistant must answer from SharePoint and Blob content. Different employees may read different files. Questions often follow earlier turns.
unknowns: Is the user token available at the retrieve call?
scenarios.question: What must be in place?

options.name: Knowledge base with `ingestionPermissionOptions` set at creation, and the user token sent in `x-ms-query-source-authorization` on every retrieve
options.why: Without both, indexed sources return unfiltered results [[r6]].
options.tradeoff: Identity plumbing and sync lag for ACL changes.

options.name: Rely on the app's own check after retrieval
options.why: Content may already be in the prompt, and results shrink unpredictably.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable as defence in depth on top of source filtering.

options.name: Use an app identity with broad read access
options.tradeoff: Everything must then be filtered elsewhere, so it breaks least privilege.

flips.then: Add a live source check on sensitive hits.

flips.if: All employees may read all the content
flips.then: Drop per-user token forwarding and use a single app identity, keeping the knowledge base simpler.

scenarios.title: Latency-sensitive lookup assistant
scenarios.situation: A support assistant answers short factual questions within a one-second retrieval budget. Some users ask two-part questions.
unknowns: What share of questions are multi-part?
scenarios.question: How do you use agentic retrieval?

options.name: Serve single-fact questions with one hybrid query, and route multi-part questions to `low` effort
options.why: Planning adds an LLM pass, so reserve it for questions that need it.
options.tradeoff: You need a router and must measure its accuracy.

options.name: Use `medium` for everything
options.why: It adds a classifier and possible retry to every query.
options.tradeoff: Right for a research assistant with no tight budget.

flips.if: The budget grows to several seconds
Two-part questions become the majority of traffic
flips.then: Route most traffic to `low` effort, and measure latency against the budget before widening it.

scenarios.takeaway: Spend planning only where questions need it.

quiz.q: A retrieve call returns documents the caller must not see, and the request carried no identity header. What is the most likely cause?
options: Indexed sources return unfiltered results when no user identity is passed
The knowledge base is at `minimal` effort
quiz.explain: Omitting the user token makes indexed sources return unfiltered results. This fails open. The other options do not remove permission trimming [[r6]].

quiz.q: Select the statements true of Azure agentic retrieval on 2026-10-13.
options: Stable `2026-04-01` supports `minimal` extractive retrieval with `intents` input
quiz.explain: Only `minimal` is in the stable API. Planning, synthesis, `auto` and SSE need the preview version [[r4]].

quiz.q: Match each effort level to its behaviour.

pairs.r: No LLM planning, searches every source
One planning pass, default if unset
Adds a semantic classifier and one retry
Starts light and escalates up to medium

quiz.explain: These are the behaviours documented for each reasoning effort [[r5]].

flashcards.front: What does agentic retrieval do at `low` effort?
flashcards.back: One LLM planning pass makes focused subqueries and picks sources. Subqueries run in parallel, are reranked and merged.

flashcards.front: Which API version holds stable agentic retrieval, and what does it allow?
flashcards.back: `2026-04-01`: `minimal` effort, `intents` input and extractive output. Planning, synthesis and SSE need `2026-08-01-preview`.

flashcards.front: How are permissions enforced in Foundry IQ indexed sources?
flashcards.back: Ingest ACLs with `ingestionPermissionOptions` and send the user token in `x-ms-query-source-authorization`. Without it results are unfiltered.
